steps.words: Why does the author think consciousness can't just be computation?
Where does he admit his case might be weak?

rows.answer: He gives four linked arguments against computational functionalism, the view that running the right computation is enough for consciousness [spya-cv97j7]. The main one is that you can't separate what a brain does from what it is [spya-p4vmm0]. The other three: much of what brains do isn't Turing computation [spya-n393ru], life may be necessary [spya-da9tvt], and simulating something doesn't create it [spya-pbcr03]. For the full case, read from "Brains Are Not Computers" [spya-sk4su6] to his recap [spya-ymbpwn].

steps.words: What does he mean by the 'mythology' of conscious AI?
techno-rapture and mind uploading

rows.answer: He never defines the word outright. He uses it for the beliefs our biases lead us into [spya-k850tu], for "ancestor simulations, mind-uploading and the like" [spya-ryg483], and for computational functionalism, an assumption so ingrained it is hard to see as one [spya-wepmnr]. For its quasi-religious side, read where uploading is called "a regression to the Cartesian soul" [spya-gvzuc4].

steps.words: Is his argument against the brain-as-computer idea actually convincing?

rows.answer:
He supports it with three main points. Brains have no clean split between software and hardware [spya-zw2m7u]. Some neurons do metabolic work that no silicon part could copy [spya-un9fjn]. And brains run in continuous time [spya-v52g4f].

My guess is that a functionalist would reply that only function at some coarser level matters. His answer is evidence that what the brain is made of matters [spya-p4vmm0]. The section starting at [spya-a8jgf4] has the full case.

steps.words: Why does the author think consciousness can't just be computation?

rows.answer:
He doesn't claim it can't be computation, only that computational functionalism, the view that the right computation is enough for consciousness, "may" be wrong [spya-wepmnr]. He gives four arguments: brains can't be separated from what they're made of [spya-zw2m7u], much of what they do lies outside algorithms [spya-n393ru], life may be necessary [spya-hj5y6s], and a simulation isn't the real thing [spya-npjt4j]. Read the four numbered sections, starting at [spya-cv97j7].
